Standards & Classics · Unit 3 · song std-blue-danube “The Blue Danube” · step 1 (explain) · title

rows.source: Johann Strauss II first performed this waltz in Vienna in 1867, and Vienna still plays it every New Year's Day. Its tune climbs a chord, then answers with two high notes.
rows.translation: Johann Strauss II frumflutti þennan vals í Vín árið 1867 og í Vín er hann enn spilaður á hverjum nýársdegi. Laglínan stígur upp hljóm og svarar svo með tveimur háum nótum.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 3 · song std-blue-danube “The Blue Danube” · step 1 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.source: G at fret 3 on string 6 twice, B on string 5, open D, then leap up to D at fret 3 on string 2 and down to open B.
rows.translation: G á bandi 3 á streng 6 tvisvar, B á streng 5, opið D og svo stökk upp að D á bandi 3 á streng 2 og niður að opnu B.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 3 · song std-blue-danube “The Blue Danube” · step 2 (notes) · hint under an exercise
Standards & Classics · Unit 3 · song std-blue-danube “The Blue Danube” · step 3 (explain) · title

rows.source: Each phrase starts low on the bass strings and leaps up an octave. Look at the high note before you play the low ones, so your hand knows where it's going.
rows.translation: Hver hending byrjar lágt á bassastrengjunum og stekkur upp um áttund. Horfðu á háa tóninn áður en þú spilar þá lágu svo höndin viti hvert hún er að fara.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 3 · song std-blue-danube “The Blue Danube” · step 3 (explain) · lesson card text

Standards & Classics · Unit 3 · song std-can-can “Can-can” · step 1 (explain) · title

rows.source: Jacques Offenbach wrote this galop for his 1858 operetta Orpheus in the Underworld. Paris dance halls later made it the music of the can-can.
rows.translation: Jacques Offenbach samdi þennan galopp fyrir óperettu sína Orfeus í undirheimum árið 1858. Danssalir Parísar gerðu hann síðar að tónlist can-can-dansins.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 3 · song std-can-can “Can-can” · step 1 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.source: A long open G, then A, C, B, A, and two Ds at fret 3 on string 2.
rows.translation: Langt opið G, svo A, C, B, A og tvö D á bandi 3 á streng 2.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 3 · song std-can-can “Can-can” · step 2 (notes) · hint under an exercise
Standards & Classics · Unit 3 · song std-can-can “Can-can” · step 3 (explain) · title

rows.source: Most of the tune runs in eighth notes. Keep the pick small and alternate down and up, so you never fall behind.
rows.translation: Mest af laginu fer í áttundapartsnótum. Hafðu naglarhreyfingarnar litlar og skiptu milli niðurstrika og uppstrika svo þú dragist aldrei aftur úr.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 3 · song std-can-can “Can-can” · step 3 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.source: The big run: open G, leap to G at fret 3 on string 1, then step all the way down to A.
rows.translation: Stóra runan: opið G, stökk að G á bandi 3 á streng 1 og svo skref alla leið niður að A.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 3 · song std-can-can “Can-can” · step 5 (notes) · hint under an exercise

Standards & Classics · Unit 3 · challenge std-medley-dances “Dance hall medley” · step 1 (explain) · title

rows.source: Four tunes from this unit: a pipe march, a Russian folk song, a Viennese waltz and a French galop. Each one a little faster than before.
rows.translation: Fjögur lög úr þessari einingu: sekkjapípumars, rússneskt þjóðlag, vínarvals og franskur galopp. Hvert aðeins hraðar en áður.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 3 · challenge std-medley-dances “Dance hall medley” · step 1 (explain) · lesson card text
Standards & Classics · Unit 3 · challenge std-medley-dances “Dance hall medley” · step 2 (listen) · question or instruction

rows.source: Which of these is a waltz, in three?
rows.translation: Hvert þessara laga er vals í þremur?
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 3 · challenge std-medley-dances “Dance hall medley” · step 5 (quiz) · question or instruction

rows.source: A waltz counts one, two, three. The can-can and the pipe march both count in four.
rows.translation: Vals telur einn, tveir, þrír. Can-can og sekkjapípumarsinn telja báðir í fjórum.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 3 · challenge std-medley-dances “Dance hall medley” · step 5 (quiz) · explanation after a quiz answer
Standards & Classics · Unit 4 “Ragtime, marches and the stage” · title

rows.source: Joplin, Sousa, Bizet and Grieg: syncopation, six-eight and key changes.
rows.translation: Joplin, Sousa, Bizet og Grieg: áherslufærsla, sex áttundaparta taktur og tóntegundaskipti.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 4 “Ragtime, marches and the stage” · unit summary
Standards & Classics · Unit 4 · song std-the-entertainer “The Entertainer” · step 1 (explain) · title

rows.source: Scott Joplin published The Entertainer in 1902, and a 1973 film made it famous again. In ragtime the tune leans off the beat while the bass keeps steady time.
rows.translation: Scott Joplin gaf The Entertainer út árið 1902 og kvikmynd frá 1973 gerði það aftur frægt. Í ragtime leitar laglínan milli slaganna á meðan bassinn heldur stöðugum takti.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 4 · song std-the-entertainer “The Entertainer” · step 1 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.source: Open D, D sharp at fret 1, E at fret 2 on string 4, then leap to C at fret 1 on string 2 and back, three times.
rows.translation: Opið D, hækkað D á bandi 1, E á bandi 2 á streng 4, svo stökk að C á bandi 1 á streng 2 og til baka, þrisvar.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 4 · song std-the-entertainer “The Entertainer” · step 2 (notes) · hint under an exercise

rows.source: Syncopation puts the accent between the beats. In the opening, each C lands on an and. Count one-and-two-and and feel the C pull ahead.
rows.translation: Áherslufærsla setur áhersluna milli slaga. Í upphafinu lendir hvert C á og. Teldu einn-og-tveir-og og finndu C leita fram á við.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 4 · song std-the-entertainer “The Entertainer” · step 3 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.source: The ending run circles C, D and E on strings 2 and 1, then lands through B and D on C.
rows.translation: Lokarunan hringsólar um C, D og E á strengjum 2 og 1 og lendir svo í gegnum B og D á C.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 4 · song std-the-entertainer “The Entertainer” · step 5 (notes) · hint under an exercise
Standards & Classics · Unit 4 · song std-the-liberty-bell “The Liberty Bell” · step 1 (explain) · title

rows.source: John Philip Sousa published The Liberty Bell in 1893, and a British TV comedy later made it its theme. It's in six-eight: two big beats a bar, like left, right.
rows.translation: John Philip Sousa gaf The Liberty Bell út árið 1893 og breskur sjónvarpsgamanþáttur gerði það síðar að stefi sínu. Það er í sex áttundaparta takti: tvö stór slög í takti, eins og vinstri, hægri.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 4 · song std-the-liberty-bell “The Liberty Bell” · step 1 (explain) · lesson card text
Standards & Classics · Unit 4 · song std-the-liberty-bell “The Liberty Bell” · step 2 (explain) · title

rows.source: Many beats start with a short silence. Stop the string with your fretting hand, then come back in on the next eighth.
rows.translation: Mörg slög byrja með stuttri þögn. Stöðvaðu strenginn með griphendinni og komdu svo aftur inn á næstu áttundapartsnótu.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 4 · song std-the-liberty-bell “The Liberty Bell” · step 2 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.source: Open B three times, A sharp at fret 3 on string 3, B again, then up to G on string 1 and down D, D, B.
rows.translation: Opið B þrisvar, hækkað A á bandi 3 á streng 3, B aftur, svo upp að G á streng 1 og niður D, D, B.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 4 · song std-the-liberty-bell “The Liberty Bell” · step 4 (notes) · hint under an exercise

Standards & Classics · Unit 4 · song std-carmen-prelude “Carmen: Prelude” · step 1 (explain) · title

rows.source: Georges Bizet's opera Carmen opened in Paris in 1875. Its prelude starts with this festive march, then plays the tune of the famous Toreador Song.
rows.translation: Óperan Carmen eftir Georges Bizet var frumsýnd í París árið 1875. Forleikurinn byrjar á þessum hátíðlega marsi og spilar svo laglínu hins fræga Nautabanasöngs.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 4 · song std-carmen-prelude “Carmen: Prelude” · step 1 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.source: Four As at fret 2 on string 3, then down to E at fret 2 on string 4, open D and E.
rows.translation: Fjögur A á bandi 2 á streng 3 og svo niður að E á bandi 2 á streng 4, opið D og E.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 4 · song std-carmen-prelude “Carmen: Prelude” · step 2 (notes) · hint under an exercise
Standards & Classics · Unit 4 · song std-carmen-prelude “Carmen: Prelude” · step 3 (explain) · title

rows.source: The march is in A major, with C sharp and G sharp. The Toreador tune moves to F major, with B flat at fret 3 on string 3. Watch for the change.
rows.translation: Marsinn er í A-dúr, með hækkuðu C og hækkuðu G. Nautabanasöngurinn færist í F-dúr, með lækkuðu B á bandi 3 á streng 3. Fylgstu með skiptunum.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 4 · song std-carmen-prelude “Carmen: Prelude” · step 3 (explain) · lesson card text
Standards & Classics · Unit 4 · song std-carmen-prelude “Carmen: Prelude” · step 5 (along) · title

rows.source: What happens at the end of the Toreador tune?
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 4 · song std-carmen-prelude “Carmen: Prelude” · step 6 (quiz) · question or instruction

rows.source: It climbs to a long E
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 4 · song std-carmen-prelude “Carmen: Prelude” · step 6 (quiz) · quiz answer
Standards & Classics · Unit 4 · song std-carmen-prelude “Carmen: Prelude” · step 6 (quiz) · quiz answer

rows.translation: Hann hægir á sér og stöðvast
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 4 · song std-carmen-prelude “Carmen: Prelude” · step 6 (quiz) · quiz answer

rows.source: It climbs to a long high E, the note that leads back home to A major for the march.
rows.translation: Hann stígur að löngu, háu E, tóninum sem leiðir aftur heim að A-dúr fyrir marsinn.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 4 · song std-carmen-prelude “Carmen: Prelude” · step 6 (quiz) · explanation after a quiz answer

Standards & Classics · Unit 4 · song std-morning-mood “Morning Mood” · title
Standards & Classics · Unit 4 · song std-morning-mood “Morning Mood” · step 1 (explain) · title

rows.source: Edvard Grieg wrote Morning Mood in 1875 for the play Peer Gynt. The flute plays the theme, the oboe answers, and the music climbs like the rising sun.
rows.translation: Edvard Grieg samdi verkið Morgunstemning árið 1875 fyrir leikritið Peer Gynt. Flautan spilar stefið, óbóið svarar og tónlistin stígur eins og rísandi sól.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 4 · song std-morning-mood “Morning Mood” · step 1 (explain) · lesson card text
Standards & Classics · Unit 4 · song std-morning-mood “Morning Mood” · step 2 (explain) · title

rows.source: The theme uses just G, A, B, D and E. A five-note scale like this is called pentatonic, and it sounds calm and open.
rows.translation: Stefið notar aðeins G, A, B, D og E. Svona fimm tóna tónstigi kallast fimmtóna tónstigi og hljómar rólegur og opinn.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 4 · song std-morning-mood “Morning Mood” · step 2 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.source: D at fret 3 on string 2, open B, A at fret 2 on string 3, open G, then back up A and B.
rows.translation: D á bandi 3 á streng 2, opið B, A á bandi 2 á streng 3, opið G og svo aftur upp A og B.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 4 · song std-morning-mood “Morning Mood” · step 3 (notes) · hint under an exercise

rows.source: How many different notes does the theme use?
rows.translation: Hve marga ólíka tóna notar stefið?
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 4 · song std-morning-mood “Morning Mood” · step 4 (quiz) · question or instruction

rows.source: G, A, B, D and E: a pentatonic scale. There is no C and no F sharp in the whole theme.
rows.translation: G, A, B, D og E: fimmtóna tónstigi. Hvorki C né hækkað F er í öllu stefinu.

rows.source: The four pieces from this unit, back to back: ragtime, a march, an opera prelude and a sunrise. Each a little faster than before.
rows.translation: Verkin fjögur úr þessari einingu hvert á eftir öðru: ragtime, mars, óperuforleikur og sólarupprás. Hvert aðeins hraðar en áður.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 4 · challenge std-medley-stage “Showstoppers medley” · step 1 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.source: Which of these pieces uses only five notes in its theme?
rows.translation: Hvert þessara verka notar aðeins fimm tóna í stefinu sínu?
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 4 · challenge std-medley-stage “Showstoppers medley” · step 5 (quiz) · question or instruction

rows.source: Morning Mood's theme is pentatonic: G, A, B, D and E. The others use many more.
rows.translation: Stefið í verkinu Morgunstemning er fimmtóna: G, A, B, D og E. Hin nota miklu fleiri.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 4 · challenge std-medley-stage “Showstoppers medley” · step 5 (quiz) · explanation after a quiz answer
Standards & Classics · Unit 5 “Carols by candlelight” · title

rows.source: Four Christmas carols to sing by candlelight: Wesley and Mendelssohn, a lullaby, and two tunes from America.
rows.translation: Fjögur jólalög við kertaljós: Wesley og Mendelssohn, vögguvísa og tvö lög frá Ameríku.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 5 “Carols by candlelight” · unit summary
Standards & Classics · Unit 5 · song std-hark-the-herald “Hark! The Herald Angels Sing” · step 1 (explain) · title

rows.source: Charles Wesley wrote the words in 1739. In 1856 an English organist set them to a tune from a choral piece by Felix Mendelssohn, and the carol has been sung that way since.
rows.translation: Charles Wesley samdi textann árið 1739. Árið 1856 setti enskur organisti hann við lag úr kórverki eftir Felix Mendelssohn og jólalagið hefur verið sungið þannig síðan.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 5 · song std-hark-the-herald “Hark! The Herald Angels Sing” · step 1 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.source: Open D, open G twice, F sharp at fret 4 on string 4, G, then open B twice and A at fret 2 on string 3.
rows.translation: Opið D, opið G tvisvar, hækkað F á bandi 4 á streng 4, G, svo opið B tvisvar og A á bandi 2 á streng 3.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 5 · song std-hark-the-herald “Hark! The Herald Angels Sing” · step 2 (notes) · hint under an exercise
Standards & Classics · Unit 5 · song std-hark-the-herald “Hark! The Herald Angels Sing” · step 3 (explain) · title

rows.source: Her-ald is long-short: her- lands on three and holds, and -ald slips in on the and of four. Count one, two, three, four-and.
rows.translation: Her-ald er langt-stutt: her- lendir á þremur og heldur, en -ald smýgur inn á og á eftir fjórum. Teldu einn, tveir, þrír, fjórir-og.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 5 · song std-hark-the-herald “Hark! The Herald Angels Sing” · step 3 (explain) · lesson card text
Standards & Classics · Unit 5 · song std-hark-the-herald “Hark! The Herald Angels Sing” · step 7 (explain) · title

rows.source: The chorus moves C, A minor, D7 and G. Change on the word that starts each half bar, and keep the strum light under the high E.
rows.translation: Viðlagið fer C, A-moll, D7 og G. Skiptu á orðinu sem byrjar hvern hálfan takt og hafðu yfirsláttinn léttan undir háa E.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 5 · song std-hark-the-herald “Hark! The Herald Angels Sing” · step 7 (explain) · lesson card text

Standards & Classics · Unit 5 · song std-away-in-a-manger “Away in a Manger” · step 1 (explain) · title

rows.source: These words first appeared in an American children's book in 1885, and James R. Murray gave them this gentle tune in 1887. It rocks in three, like a cradle.
rows.translation: Þessi texti birtist fyrst í bandarískri barnabók árið 1885 og James R. Murray samdi þetta milda lag við hann árið 1887. Það ruggar í þremur eins og vagga.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 5 · song std-away-in-a-manger “Away in a Manger” · step 1 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.source: It starts high: D at fret 3 on string 2, then steps down C, B, A, G and F sharp all the way to open D.
rows.translation: Það byrjar hátt: D á bandi 3 á streng 2 og fer svo niður C, B, A, G og hækkað F alla leið að opnu D.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 5 · song std-away-in-a-manger “Away in a Manger” · step 2 (notes) · hint under an exercise

rows.source: The first line walks down from high D to low D. How far is that?
rows.translation: Fyrsta línan gengur niður frá háu D að lágu D. Hve langt er það?
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 5 · song std-away-in-a-manger “Away in a Manger” · step 5 (quiz) · question or instruction

rows.source: D down to D is an octave: eight steps of the scale, the same note name, one register lower.
rows.translation: D niður að D er áttund: átta skref tónstigans, sama tónheiti, einu tónsviði neðar.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 5 · song std-away-in-a-manger “Away in a Manger” · step 5 (quiz) · explanation after a quiz answer

rows.source: Hold G for most of a line, C for crib for a bed, and D7 to lead home. In three, strum down on one and lightly on two and three.
rows.translation: Haltu G mestalla línuna, C fyrir crib for a bed og D7 til að leiða heim. Í þremur skaltu slá niður á einu og létt á tveimur og þremur.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 5 · song std-away-in-a-manger “Away in a Manger” · step 6 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.translation: Óþekktur höfundur (1885); erindi 3 John T. McFarland (1892)
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 5 · song std-away-in-a-manger “Away in a Manger” · arrangement · lyric credit (a name and year: usually keep as is)
Standards & Classics · Unit 5 · song std-o-little-town “O Little Town of Bethlehem” · step 1 (explain) · title

rows.source: Phillips Brooks wrote these words in 1868 for the children of his Philadelphia church, and its organist, Lewis Redner, wrote the tune for their Christmas service.
rows.translation: Phillips Brooks samdi þennan texta árið 1868 fyrir börnin í kirkju sinni í Fíladelfíu og organistinn þar, Lewis Redner, samdi lagið fyrir jólaguðsþjónustu þeirra.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 5 · song std-o-little-town “O Little Town of Bethlehem” · step 1 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.source: Open B three times, A sharp at fret 3 on string 3, B again, then D, C and a drop to E on string 4.
rows.translation: Opið B þrisvar, hækkað A á bandi 3 á streng 3, B aftur, svo D, C og niður að E á streng 4.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 5 · song std-o-little-town “O Little Town of Bethlehem” · step 2 (notes) · hint under an exercise
Standards & Classics · Unit 5 · song std-o-little-town “O Little Town of Bethlehem” · step 3 (explain) · title

rows.source: A sharp at fret 3 on string 3 leans into open B, a half step up. It gives O little town its gentle sway.
rows.translation: Hækkað A á bandi 3 á streng 3 leitar að opnu B, hálftónsskrefi ofar. Það gefur O little town milda sveiflu sína.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 5 · song std-o-little-town “O Little Town of Bethlehem” · step 3 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.source: Which word dips down to the low D in the first verse?
rows.translation: Hvaða orð fer niður að lága D í fyrsta erindi?
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 5 · song std-o-little-town “O Little Town of Bethlehem” · step 5 (quiz) · question or instruction

rows.source: Thee, in how still we see thee lie
rows.translation: Thee, í how still we see thee lie
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 5 · song std-o-little-town “O Little Town of Bethlehem” · step 5 (quiz) · quiz answer

rows.source: How still we see thee lie: the tune falls to open D on thee, then lifts to B on lie.
rows.translation: How still we see thee lie: laglínan fellur að opnu D á thee og lyftist svo að B á lie.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 5 · song std-o-little-town “O Little Town of Bethlehem” · step 5 (quiz) · explanation after a quiz answer
Standards & Classics · Unit 5 · song std-it-came-upon “It Came Upon the Midnight Clear” · step 1 (explain) · title

rows.source: Edmund Sears wrote these words in Massachusetts in 1849, and Richard Storrs Willis wrote the tune a year later. It swings in two big beats a bar, each split in three.
rows.translation: Edmund Sears samdi þennan texta í Massachusetts árið 1849 og Richard Storrs Willis samdi lagið ári síðar. Það sveiflast í tveimur stórum slögum í takti, hvoru skipt í þrennt.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 5 · song std-it-came-upon “It Came Upon the Midnight Clear” · step 1 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.source: In six-eight a quarter and an eighth make one big beat: long, short. Count one-two-three, four-five-six, and play on one, three, four and six.
rows.translation: Í sex áttundaparta takti mynda fjórðapartsnóta og áttundapartsnóta eitt stórt slag: langt, stutt. Teldu einn-tveir-þrír, fjórir-fimm-sex og spilaðu á einu, þremur, fjórum og sex.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 5 · song std-it-came-upon “It Came Upon the Midnight Clear” · step 2 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.source: Open G, a leap to open E on string 1, then B, D, C, A, and back to G with a turn through A.
rows.translation: Opið G, stökk að opnu E á streng 1, svo B, D, C, A og aftur að G með sveig um A.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 5 · song std-it-came-upon “It Came Upon the Midnight Clear” · step 4 (notes) · hint under an exercise

rows.source: The middle of the verse drops to low E and climbs through G sharp, at fret 1 on string 3, to A. Under it the chord moves from E7 to A minor.
rows.translation: Miðja erindisins fellur að lágu E og stígur í gegnum hækkað G á bandi 1 á streng 3 að A. Undir færist hljómurinn frá E7 í A-moll.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 5 · song std-it-came-upon “It Came Upon the Midnight Clear” · step 6 (explain) · lesson card text
Standards & Classics · Unit 5 · challenge std-medley-carols “Carol medley” · title
Standards & Classics · Unit 5 · challenge std-medley-carols “Carol medley” · step 1 (explain) · title

rows.source: The four carols from this unit, one after another, each a little faster. Keep the chords soft and let the tune sing.
rows.translation: Jólalögin fjögur úr þessari einingu, hvert á eftir öðru, aðeins hraðar. Hafðu hljómana mjúka og láttu laglínuna syngja.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 5 · challenge std-medley-carols “Carol medley” · step 1 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.source: Which of these carols counts in three?
rows.translation: Hvert þessara jólalaga telur í þremur?
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 5 · challenge std-medley-carols “Carol medley” · step 5 (quiz) · question or instruction

rows.source: Away in a Manger is a waltz: one, two, three. The other two count in four.
rows.translation: Away in a Manger er vals: einn, tveir, þrír. Hin tvö telja í fjórum.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 5 · challenge std-medley-carols “Carol medley” · step 5 (quiz) · explanation after a quiz answer
Standards & Classics · Unit 6 “Winter carols” · title

rows.source: King's College's opening carol, Holst's midwinter carol, a folk carol and a grand processional.
rows.translation: Upphafsjólalag King's College, miðvetrarlag Holsts, þjóðlegt jólalag og tignarlegt skrúðgöngulag.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 6 “Winter carols” · unit summary
Standards & Classics · Unit 6 · song std-royal-davids-city “Once in Royal David's City” · step 1 (explain) · title

rows.source: Cecil Frances Alexander wrote these words for children in 1848. Since 1919 a single young voice has sung the first verse to open the Christmas Eve carols at King's College, Cambridge.
rows.translation: Cecil Frances Alexander samdi þennan texta fyrir börn árið 1848. Frá 1919 hefur ein ung rödd sungið fyrsta erindið til að opna jólasönginn á aðfangadagskvöld í King's College í Cambridge.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 6 · song std-royal-davids-city “Once in Royal David's City” · step 1 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.source: Open D, F sharp at fret 4 on string 4, open G, then a turn: G, F sharp, G, A, A, G.
rows.translation: Opið D, hækkað F á bandi 4 á streng 4, opið G og svo sveigur: G, hækkað F, G, A, A, G.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 6 · song std-royal-davids-city “Once in Royal David's City” · step 2 (notes) · hint under an exercise
Standards & Classics · Unit 6 · song std-royal-davids-city “Once in Royal David's City” · step 3 (explain) · title

rows.source: Da-vid's spreads each syllable over two eighth notes. Play both, but sing them as one smooth sound.
rows.translation: Da-vid's dreifir hvoru atkvæði yfir tvær áttundapartsnótur. Spilaðu báðar en syngdu þær sem eitt mjúkt hljóð.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 6 · song std-royal-davids-city “Once in Royal David's City” · step 3 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.source: Where is the highest note of the carol?
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 6 · song std-royal-davids-city “Once in Royal David's City” · step 5 (quiz) · question or instruction

Standards & Classics · Unit 6 · song std-royal-davids-city “Once in Royal David's City” · step 5 (quiz) · quiz answer

rows.source: Mary was that mother mild starts on open E, the top of the tune.
rows.translation: Mary was that mother mild byrjar á opnu E, efsta tóni lagsins.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 6 · song std-royal-davids-city “Once in Royal David's City” · step 5 (quiz) · explanation after a quiz answer

rows.source: A poem and a quiet tune
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 6 · song std-bleak-midwinter “In the Bleak Midwinter” · step 1 (explain) · title

rows.source: Christina Rossetti wrote this poem in 1872, and Gustav Holst set it to music for a hymn book in 1906. Its lines are short and calm, like snow falling.
rows.translation: Christina Rossetti samdi þetta ljóð árið 1872 og Gustav Holst samdi lag við það fyrir sálmabók árið 1906. Línurnar eru stuttar og rólegar eins og fallandi snjór.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 6 · song std-bleak-midwinter “In the Bleak Midwinter” · step 1 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.source: Open B twice, C at fret 1 and D at fret 3 on string 2, then back down B, A and G.
rows.translation: Opið B tvisvar, C á bandi 1 og D á bandi 3 á streng 2 og svo aftur niður B, A og G.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 6 · song std-bleak-midwinter “In the Bleak Midwinter” · step 2 (notes) · hint under an exercise
Standards & Classics · Unit 6 · song std-bleak-midwinter “In the Bleak Midwinter” · step 3 (explain) · title

rows.source: Many words land on half notes: -ter in mid-winter, i-ron. Let each ring for two full beats before you move on.
rows.translation: Mörg orð lenda á hálfnótum: -ter í mid-winter, i-ron. Láttu hvert hljóma í tvö heil slög áður en þú heldur áfram.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 6 · song std-bleak-midwinter “In the Bleak Midwinter” · step 3 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.source: Long ago stretches three syllables over how many notes?
rows.translation: Yfir hve margar nótur teygir Long ago atkvæðin þrjú?
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 6 · song std-bleak-midwinter “In the Bleak Midwinter” · step 5 (quiz) · question or instruction

rows.source: Long takes two notes, a- takes two, and go takes one: five notes for three syllables.
rows.translation: Long tekur tvær nótur, a- tekur tvær og go tekur eina: fimm nótur fyrir þrjú atkvæði.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 6 · song std-bleak-midwinter “In the Bleak Midwinter” · step 5 (quiz) · explanation after a quiz answer
Standards & Classics · Unit 6 · song std-bleak-midwinter “In the Bleak Midwinter” · step 6 (explain) · title

rows.source: Under frost-y wind made moan the chords move A minor to D7, a lean that pulls the line back to G.
rows.translation: Undir frost-y wind made moan færast hljómarnir frá A-moll að D7, hreyfing sem dregur línuna aftur að G.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 6 · song std-bleak-midwinter “In the Bleak Midwinter” · step 6 (explain) · lesson card text
Standards & Classics · Unit 6 · song std-holly-and-ivy “The Holly and the Ivy” · step 1 (explain) · title

rows.source: This carol is centuries old. The song collector Cecil Sharp heard it sung in a Cotswold town and printed this tune in 1911. It dances in three.
rows.translation: Þetta jólalag er margra alda gamalt. Þjóðlagasafnarinn Cecil Sharp heyrði það sungið í bæ í Cotswolds og prentaði þetta lag árið 1911. Það dansar í þremur.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 6 · song std-holly-and-ivy “The Holly and the Ivy” · step 1 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.source: Four open Gs, then a leap to open E on string 1, down to D at fret 3 on string 2 and open B.
rows.translation: Fjögur opin G, svo stökk að opnu E á streng 1, niður að D á bandi 3 á streng 2 og opnu B.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 6 · song std-holly-and-ivy “The Holly and the Ivy” · step 2 (notes) · hint under an exercise
Standards & Classics · Unit 6 · song std-holly-and-ivy “The Holly and the Ivy” · step 3 (explain) · title

rows.source: From open G to open E is a sixth. Keep your pick close to the strings and cross from string 3 to string 1 in one move.
rows.translation: Frá opnu G að opnu E er sexund. Haltu nöglinni nálægt strengjunum og farðu frá streng 3 að streng 1 í einni hreyfingu.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 6 · song std-holly-and-ivy “The Holly and the Ivy” · step 3 (explain) · lesson card text
Standards & Classics · Unit 6 · song std-holly-and-ivy “The Holly and the Ivy” · arrangement · lyric credit (a name and year: usually keep as is)
Standards & Classics · Unit 6 · song std-angels-from-the-realms “Angels from the Realms of Glory” · step 1 (explain) · title

rows.source: James Montgomery printed these words in his Sheffield newspaper on Christmas Eve, 1816. Henry Smart's tune, from 1867, gives it a grand, marching sound.
rows.translation: James Montgomery prentaði þennan texta í dagblaði sínu í Sheffield á aðfangadagskvöld árið 1816. Lag Henry Smart frá 1867 gefur honum tignarlegan marssvip.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 6 · song std-angels-from-the-realms “Angels from the Realms of Glory” · step 1 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.source: A on string 3, F sharp at fret 4 on string 4, D at fret 3 on string 2, A, then F sharp at fret 2 on string 1, E and D.
rows.translation: A á streng 3, hækkað F á bandi 4 á streng 4, D á bandi 3 á streng 2, A og svo hækkað F á bandi 2 á streng 1, E og D.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 6 · song std-angels-from-the-realms “Angels from the Realms of Glory” · step 2 (notes) · hint under an exercise
Standards & Classics · Unit 6 · song std-angels-from-the-realms “Angels from the Realms of Glory” · step 3 (explain) · title

rows.source: This key has two sharps, F sharp and C sharp. C sharp sits at fret 2 on string 2.
rows.translation: Þessi tóntegund hefur tvo krossa, hækkað F og hækkað C. Hækkað C situr á bandi 2 á streng 2.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 6 · song std-angels-from-the-realms “Angels from the Realms of Glory” · step 3 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.source: Where is the highest note of the chorus?
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 6 · song std-angels-from-the-realms “Angels from the Realms of Glory” · step 6 (quiz) · question or instruction
Standards & Classics · Unit 6 · song std-angels-from-the-realms “Angels from the Realms of Glory” · step 6 (quiz) · quiz answer
Standards & Classics · Unit 6 · song std-angels-from-the-realms “Angels from the Realms of Glory” · step 6 (quiz) · quiz answer

rows.source: Worship Christ starts on G at fret 3 on string 1, the top of the whole carol.
rows.translation: Worship Christ byrjar á G á bandi 3 á streng 1, efsta tóni alls jólalagsins.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 6 · song std-angels-from-the-realms “Angels from the Realms of Glory” · step 6 (quiz) · explanation after a quiz answer

Standards & Classics · Unit 6 · challenge std-medley-winter “Winter medley” · step 1 (explain) · title

rows.source: The carols from this unit, back to back. Most move in long notes: let each one ring full length before the next.
rows.translation: Jólalögin úr þessari einingu, hvert á eftir öðru. Flest fara í löngum nótum: láttu hverja hljóma alla sína lengd áður en sú næsta kemur.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 6 · challenge std-medley-winter “Winter medley” · step 1 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.source: Which of these counts in three?
rows.translation: Hvert þessara laga telur í þremur?
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 6 · challenge std-medley-winter “Winter medley” · step 5 (quiz) · question or instruction

rows.source: The Holly and the Ivy is in three. The other two count in four.
rows.translation: The Holly and the Ivy er í þremur. Hin tvö telja í fjórum.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 6 · challenge std-medley-winter “Winter medley” · step 5 (quiz) · explanation after a quiz answer
Standards & Classics · Unit 7 “Hymns everyone knows” · title

rows.source: Five great hymns in long, singing notes, from 1708 to 1861.
rows.translation: Fimm stórir sálmar í löngum, syngjandi nótum, frá 1708 til 1861.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 7 “Hymns everyone knows” · unit summary
Standards & Classics · Unit 7 · song std-o-god-our-help “O God, Our Help in Ages Past” · step 1 (explain) · title

rows.source: William Croft wrote this tune, St Anne, in 1708, and Isaac Watts's words were first printed in 1719. Each verse is four short lines, the plainest hymn shape there is.
rows.translation: William Croft samdi þetta lag, St Anne, árið 1708 og texti Isaac Watts var fyrst prentaður árið 1719. Hvert erindi er fjórar stuttar línur, einfaldasta sálmaform sem til er.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 7 · song std-o-god-our-help “O God, Our Help in Ages Past” · step 1 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.source: Open G, E at fret 2 on string 4, A at fret 2 on string 3, G, then C at fret 1 on string 2, C, open B and C.
rows.translation: Opið G, E á bandi 2 á streng 4, A á bandi 2 á streng 3, G og svo C á bandi 1 á streng 2, C, opið B og C.

rows.source: Every line starts on the beat before the bar: O, our, our, and. Count four, then sing the first word on it.
rows.translation: Hver lína byrjar á slaginu fyrir taktinn: O, our, our, and. Teldu fjóra og syngdu fyrsta orðið þar.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 7 · song std-o-god-our-help “O God, Our Help in Ages Past” · step 3 (explain) · lesson card text
Standards & Classics · Unit 7 · song std-o-god-our-help “O God, Our Help in Ages Past” · step 5 (explain) · title

rows.source: The chart leans on A minor, F and G7. God, our sits on A minor, and a-ges past moves from G7 to C.
rows.translation: Hljómamyndin styðst við A-moll, F og G7. God, our hvílir á A-moll og a-ges past færist frá G7 að C.

rows.source: Reginald Heber wrote these words, printed in 1826, and John Bacchus Dykes wrote the tune in 1861. Its first line climbs the notes of a G major chord.
rows.translation: Reginald Heber samdi þennan texta sem var prentaður árið 1826 og John Bacchus Dykes samdi lagið árið 1861. Fyrsta línan stígur upp tóna G-dúrhljóms.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 7 · song std-holy-holy-holy “Holy, Holy, Holy” · step 1 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.source: Up the G chord: open G twice, open B twice, then D at fret 3 on string 2, held long.
rows.translation: Upp G-hljóminn: opið G tvisvar, opið B tvisvar og svo D á bandi 3 á streng 2, haldið lengi.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 7 · song std-holy-holy-holy “Holy, Holy, Holy” · step 2 (notes) · hint under an exercise

rows.source: Holy, holy, holy climbs which notes?
rows.translation: Upp hvaða tóna stígur Holy, holy, holy?

rows.source: G, B and D are the notes of a G major chord, so the tune climbs the chord itself.
rows.translation: G, B og D eru tónar G-dúrhljóms svo laglínan stígur upp hljóminn sjálfan.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 7 · song std-holy-holy-holy “Holy, Holy, Holy” · step 3 (quiz) · explanation after a quiz answer
Standards & Classics · Unit 7 · song std-holy-holy-holy “Holy, Holy, Holy” · step 5 (explain) · title

rows.source: This hymn moves in long notes: halves of two beats and a whole note of four at the end. Count every beat, even while a note rings.
rows.translation: Þessi sálmur fer í löngum nótum: tveggja slaga hálfnótum og fjögurra slaga heilnótu í lokin. Teldu hvert slag, líka á meðan nóta hljómar.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 7 · song std-holy-holy-holy “Holy, Holy, Holy” · step 5 (explain) · lesson card text
Standards & Classics · Unit 7 · song std-abide-with-me “Abide with Me” · step 1 (explain) · title

rows.source: Henry Francis Lyte wrote these words in 1847, and William Henry Monk wrote the tune Eventide for them in 1861. Football crowds in England have sung it before the cup final since 1927.
rows.translation: Henry Francis Lyte samdi þennan texta árið 1847 og William Henry Monk samdi lagið Eventide við hann árið 1861. Knattspyrnuáhorfendur á Englandi hafa sungið hann fyrir úrslitaleik bikarsins frá 1927.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 7 · song std-abide-with-me “Abide with Me” · step 1 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.source: Open B twice, A at fret 2 on string 3, open G, then D at fret 3 and E on string 1, back through D and C to B.
rows.translation: Opið B tvisvar, A á bandi 2 á streng 3, opið G, svo D á bandi 3 og E á streng 1, aftur í gegnum D og C að B.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 7 · song std-abide-with-me “Abide with Me” · step 2 (notes) · hint under an exercise
Standards & Classics · Unit 7 · song std-abide-with-me “Abide with Me” · step 3 (explain) · title

rows.source: Every note here is a quarter, a half or a whole. Count four steady beats a bar and let the long notes ring.
rows.translation: Hver nóta hér er fjórðapartsnóta, hálfnóta eða heilnóta. Teldu fjögur stöðug slög í takti og láttu löngu nóturnar hljóma.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 7 · song std-abide-with-me “Abide with Me” · step 3 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.source: Which note leads into the D at the end of the second line?
rows.translation: Hvaða tónn leiðir inn í D í lok annarrar línu?
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 7 · song std-abide-with-me “Abide with Me” · step 5 (quiz) · question or instruction

rows.source: C sharp, at fret 2 on string 2, rises a half step into D, the way a leading note does.
rows.translation: Hækkað C á bandi 2 á streng 2 rís um hálftónsskref að D, eins og leiðsögutónn gerir.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 7 · song std-abide-with-me “Abide with Me” · step 5 (quiz) · explanation after a quiz answer
Standards & Classics · Unit 7 · song std-nearer-my-god “Nearer, My God, to Thee” · step 1 (explain) · title

rows.source: Sarah Flower Adams wrote these words in London in 1841, and Lowell Mason, an American music teacher, gave them this tune in 1856.
rows.translation: Sarah Flower Adams samdi þennan texta í London árið 1841 og Lowell Mason, bandarískur tónlistarkennari, samdi þetta lag við hann árið 1856.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 7 · song std-nearer-my-god “Nearer, My God, to Thee” · step 1 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.source: Open B, A at fret 2 on string 3, open G twice, then E at fret 2 on string 4 twice.
rows.translation: Opið B, A á bandi 2 á streng 3, opið G tvisvar og svo E á bandi 2 á streng 4 tvisvar.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 7 · song std-nearer-my-god “Nearer, My God, to Thee” · step 2 (notes) · hint under an exercise
Standards & Classics · Unit 7 · song std-nearer-my-god “Nearer, My God, to Thee” · step 3 (explain) · title

rows.source: Each line has a long-short pair: a dotted quarter, then a quick eighth, as in -er, my and God, to. Let the long note lean into the short one.
rows.translation: Hver lína hefur langt-stutt par: punktaða fjórðapartsnótu og svo stutta áttundapartsnótu, eins og í -er, my og God, to. Láttu löngu nótuna leita inn í þá stuttu.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 7 · song std-nearer-my-god “Nearer, My God, to Thee” · step 3 (explain) · lesson card text
Standards & Classics · Unit 7 · song std-for-the-beauty “For the Beauty of the Earth” · step 1 (explain) · title

rows.source: Folliott Pierpoint wrote these words in 1864, on a spring day in the English countryside. They are sung to Dix, a German tune from 1838.
rows.translation: Folliott Pierpoint samdi þennan texta árið 1864 á vordegi í enskri sveit. Hann er sunginn við Dix, þýskt lag frá 1838.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 7 · song std-for-the-beauty “For the Beauty of the Earth” · step 1 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.source: Open G, F sharp at fret 4 on string 4, G, A at fret 2 on string 3, G, then C at fret 1 on string 2 twice and open B.
rows.translation: Opið G, hækkað F á bandi 4 á streng 4, G, A á bandi 2 á streng 3, G, svo C á bandi 1 á streng 2 tvisvar og opið B.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 7 · song std-for-the-beauty “For the Beauty of the Earth” · step 2 (notes) · hint under an exercise
Standards & Classics · Unit 7 · song std-for-the-beauty “For the Beauty of the Earth” · step 3 (explain) · title

rows.source: For the starts with two eighth notes on the: F sharp and G, one syllable sung over both. Play them evenly inside one beat.
rows.translation: For the byrjar með tveimur áttundapartsnótum á the: hækkuðu F og G, eitt atkvæði sungið yfir báðar. Spilaðu þær jafnt innan eins slags.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 7 · song std-for-the-beauty “For the Beauty of the Earth” · step 3 (explain) · lesson card text

Standards & Classics · Unit 7 · challenge std-medley-hymns “Hymn medley” · step 1 (explain) · title

rows.source: The hymns from this unit, back to back, from the oldest tune to the newest. Let the long notes ring and the chords change on the word.
rows.translation: Sálmarnir úr þessari einingu, hver á eftir öðrum, frá elsta laginu að því nýjasta. Láttu löngu nóturnar hljóma og hljómana skipta á orðinu.

rows.source: Which of these tunes is the oldest?
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 7 · challenge std-medley-hymns “Hymn medley” · step 5 (quiz) · question or instruction

rows.source: William Croft wrote St Anne in 1708, almost 150 years before the other two.
rows.translation: William Croft samdi St Anne árið 1708, næstum 150 árum á undan hinum tveimur.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 7 · challenge std-medley-hymns “Hymn medley” · step 5 (quiz) · explanation after a quiz answer
Standards & Classics · Unit 8 “Parlor songs and a planet” · title

rows.source: Three songs families sang around the piano, then Holst's Jupiter.
rows.translation: Þrjú lög sem fjölskyldur sungu við píanóið og svo Júpíter eftir Holst.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 8 “Parlor songs and a planet” · unit summary
Standards & Classics · Unit 8 · song std-home-sweet-home “Home! Sweet Home!” · step 1 (explain) · title

rows.source: Henry Bishop wrote this tune for a London opera in 1823, to words by the American actor John Howard Payne. Within a few years it was one of the best-loved songs in the world.
rows.translation: Henry Bishop samdi þetta lag fyrir óperu í London árið 1823 við texta bandaríska leikarans John Howard Payne. Innan fárra ára var það eitt ástsælasta lag heims.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 8 · song std-home-sweet-home “Home! Sweet Home!” · step 1 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.source: Open G, A at fret 2 on string 3, open B, C at fret 1 and D at fret 3 on string 2, then back to B.
rows.translation: Opið G, A á bandi 2 á streng 3, opið B, C á bandi 1 og D á bandi 3 á streng 2 og svo aftur að B.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 8 · song std-home-sweet-home “Home! Sweet Home!” · step 2 (notes) · hint under an exercise
Standards & Classics · Unit 8 · song std-home-sweet-home “Home! Sweet Home!” · step 3 (explain) · title

rows.source: The verse starts just before beat one, on a dotted eighth and a sixteenth. Count four-e-and-a: 'Mid lands on four, and its short turn on a.
rows.translation: Erindið byrjar rétt fyrir fyrsta slag á punktaðri áttundapartsnótu og sextándapartsnótu. Teldu fjórir-e-og-a: 'Mid lendir á fjórum og stutti sveigurinn á a.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 8 · song std-home-sweet-home “Home! Sweet Home!” · step 3 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.source: The chorus begins on one long note. How long is it?
rows.translation: Viðlagið byrjar á einni langri nótu. Hve löng er hún?
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 8 · song std-home-sweet-home “Home! Sweet Home!” · step 6 (quiz) · question or instruction

rows.source: Home! is a whole note: hold D at fret 3 on string 2 for the whole bar.
rows.translation: Home! er heilnóta: haltu D á bandi 3 á streng 2 allan taktinn.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 8 · song std-home-sweet-home “Home! Sweet Home!” · step 6 (quiz) · explanation after a quiz answer
Standards & Classics · Unit 8 · song std-hard-times “Hard Times Come Again No More” · step 1 (explain) · title

rows.source: Stephen Foster published this song in 1854. It asks the listener to stop and think of people who have less, and singers still return to it today.
rows.translation: Stephen Foster gaf þetta lag út árið 1854. Það biður hlustandann að staldra við og hugsa um þá sem eiga minna og söngvarar snúa enn aftur að því í dag.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 8 · song std-hard-times “Hard Times Come Again No More” · step 1 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.source: Open D, E and F sharp on string 4, three more F sharps, then A at fret 2 on string 3 and back to F sharp.
rows.translation: Opið D, E og hækkað F á streng 4, þrjú hækkuð F í viðbót og svo A á bandi 2 á streng 3 og aftur að hækkuðu F.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 8 · song std-hard-times “Hard Times Come Again No More” · step 2 (notes) · hint under an exercise
Standards & Classics · Unit 8 · song std-hard-times “Hard Times Come Again No More” · step 3 (explain) · title

rows.source: The verse sings several words on one note. Keep each F sharp short and even, and let the words carry the line.
rows.translation: Erindið syngur nokkur orð á einum tóni. Hafðu hvert hækkað F stutt og jafnt og láttu orðin bera línuna.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 8 · song std-hard-times “Hard Times Come Again No More” · step 3 (explain) · lesson card text
Standards & Classics · Unit 8 · song std-hard-times “Hard Times Come Again No More” · step 6 (explain) · title

rows.source: The chorus lifts to G under the long note on wear-y, then rests on D for hard times. A7 brings each line home.
rows.translation: Viðlagið lyftist í G undir löngu nótunni á wear-y og hvílir svo á D fyrir hard times. A7 færir hverja línu heim.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 8 · song std-hard-times “Hard Times Come Again No More” · step 6 (explain) · lesson card text
Standards & Classics · Unit 8 · song std-last-rose “The Last Rose of Summer” · step 1 (explain) · title

rows.source: Thomas Moore set these words to an old Irish air and printed them in 1813. Later, Mendelssohn wrote a fantasia on the tune, and Flotow put it in his opera Martha.
rows.translation: Thomas Moore setti þennan texta við gamalt írskt lag og prentaði hann árið 1813. Síðar samdi Mendelssohn fantasíu við lagið og Flotow setti það í óperu sína Martha.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 8 · song std-last-rose “The Last Rose of Summer” · step 1 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.source: Open D, E and F sharp on string 4, then a leap to D at fret 3 on string 2, and down C sharp, B and A.
rows.translation: Opið D, E og hækkað F á streng 4, svo stökk að D á bandi 3 á streng 2 og niður hækkað C, B og A.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 8 · song std-last-rose “The Last Rose of Summer” · step 2 (notes) · hint under an exercise
Standards & Classics · Unit 8 · song std-last-rose “The Last Rose of Summer” · step 3 (explain) · title

rows.source: Most beats split long-short: a dotted eighth and a sixteenth. Play the long note full and let the short one lead into the next beat.
rows.translation: Flest slög skiptast langt-stutt: punktuð áttundapartsnóta og sextándapartsnóta. Spilaðu löngu nótuna alla leið og láttu þá stuttu leiða inn í næsta slag.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 8 · song std-last-rose “The Last Rose of Summer” · step 3 (explain) · lesson card text
Standards & Classics · Unit 8 · song std-last-rose “The Last Rose of Summer” · step 6 (explain) · title

rows.source: In the middle, no rosebud is nigh climbs through A sharp to B. The chord turns to B minor there, the saddest moment of the song.
rows.translation: Í miðjunni stígur no rosebud is nigh í gegnum hækkað A að B. Hljómurinn snýr þar í B-moll, daprasta augnablik lagsins.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 8 · song std-last-rose “The Last Rose of Summer” · step 6 (explain) · lesson card text
Standards & Classics · Unit 8 · song std-jupiter “Jupiter” · title
Standards & Classics · Unit 8 · song std-jupiter “Jupiter” · step 1 (explain) · title

rows.source: Gustav Holst wrote The Planets between 1914 and 1916. This broad tune is the heart of Jupiter. In 1921 he made it a hymn tune and named it Thaxted, after the town where he lived.
rows.translation: Gustav Holst samdi Pláneturnar á milli 1914 og 1916. Þessi breiða laglína er hjarta verksins Júpíter. Árið 1921 gerði hann hana að sálmalagi og nefndi Thaxted eftir bænum þar sem hann bjó.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 8 · song std-jupiter “Jupiter” · step 1 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.source: E at fret 2 on string 4, open G, A at fret 2, then C at fret 1 on string 2, open B, G, and up C, D, C, B.
rows.translation: E á bandi 2 á streng 4, opið G, A á bandi 2, svo C á bandi 1 á streng 2, opið B, G og upp C, D, C, B.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 8 · song std-jupiter “Jupiter” · step 2 (notes) · hint under an exercise
Standards & Classics · Unit 8 · song std-jupiter “Jupiter” · step 3 (explain) · title

rows.source: The middle of the tune dips to C at fret 3 on string 5. Reach for it with your third finger, then come straight back up to string 4.
rows.translation: Miðja lagsins fer niður að C á bandi 3 á streng 5. Náðu því með baugfingri og komdu svo beint aftur upp að streng 4.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 8 · song std-jupiter “Jupiter” · step 3 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.translation: Hvernig er laglínan í verkinu Júpíter talin?

rows.source: Like a slow waltz: one, two, three. Each phrase starts with two eighth notes before beat one.
rows.translation: Eins og hægur vals: einn, tveir, þrír. Hver hending byrjar með tveimur áttundapartsnótum fyrir fyrsta slag.

rows.source: Before records, families sang these songs around the piano at home. Here they are back to back, with Holst's big tune to finish.
rows.translation: Áður en hljómplötur komu sungu fjölskyldur þessi lög við píanóið heima. Hér koma þau hvert á eftir öðru með stóru laglínu Holsts í lokin.

rows.source: Which two of these count in three?
rows.translation: Hvaða tvö þessara laga telja í þremur?

rows.source: The Last Rose of Summer and Jupiter
rows.translation: The Last Rose of Summer og Júpíter

rows.source: The Last Rose of Summer and Jupiter are both in three. Home! Sweet Home! and Hard Times count in four.

rows.source: Vivaldi's Spring, Mozart's Turkish rondo and Sousa's best-known march.
rows.translation: Vorið eftir Vivaldi, tyrkneskt rondó Mozarts og þekktasti mars Sousa.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 9 “Concert favorites” · unit summary
Standards & Classics · Unit 9 · song std-spring “Spring” · title
Standards & Classics · Unit 9 · song std-spring “Spring” · step 1 (explain) · title

rows.source: Antonio Vivaldi published four violin concertos called The Four Seasons in 1725. Spring opens with this bright tune, then the solo violin plays birdsong and running brooks.
rows.translation: Antonio Vivaldi gaf út fjóra fiðlukonserta sem kallast Árstíðirnar fjórar árið 1725. Verkið Vorið byrjar á þessari björtu laglínu og svo spilar einleiksfiðlan fuglasöng og rennandi læki.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 9 · song std-spring “Spring” · step 1 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.source: E at fret 2 on string 4, G sharp at fret 1 on string 3 three times, F sharp at fret 4 on string 4, E, then open B.
rows.translation: E á bandi 2 á streng 4, hækkað G á bandi 1 á streng 3 þrisvar, hækkað F á bandi 4 á streng 4, E og svo opið B.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 9 · song std-spring “Spring” · step 2 (notes) · hint under an exercise

rows.source: The key of E has four sharps. In first position G sharp is at fret 1 on string 3, D sharp at fret 1 on string 4, and C sharp at fret 2 on string 2.
rows.translation: Tóntegundin E hefur fjóra krossa. Í fyrstu stöðu er hækkað G á bandi 1 á streng 3, hækkað D á bandi 1 á streng 4 og hækkað C á bandi 2 á streng 2.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 9 · song std-spring “Spring” · step 3 (explain) · lesson card text
Standards & Classics · Unit 9 · song std-spring “Spring” · step 4 (explain) · title

rows.source: Each beat can split into four sixteenths. In the theme, the quick F sharp, E pair falls in the second half of beat two.
rows.translation: Hvert slag má skipta í fjórar sextándapartsnótur. Í stefinu lendir stutta parið hækkað F, E í seinni helmingi annars slags.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 9 · song std-spring “Spring” · step 4 (explain) · lesson card text

Standards & Classics · Unit 9 · song std-rondo-alla-turca “Rondo alla Turca” · step 1 (explain) · title

rows.source: Mozart published this rondo in 1784 as the last movement of a piano sonata. Its march copies the sound of Turkish military bands, which Vienna loved at the time.
rows.translation: Mozart gaf þetta rondó út árið 1784 sem síðasta þátt píanósónötu. Marsinn líkir eftir hljómi tyrkneskra herhljómsveita sem Vínarbúar voru hrifnir af á þeim tíma.
rows.context: Standards & Classics · Unit 9 · song std-rondo-alla-turca “Rondo alla Turca” · step 1 (explain) · lesson card text

rows.context: Bass Songbook course · course subtitle

rows.source: Roots and fifths, as a bass player first backs a band: the chord's root where it starts, its fifth between, low in first position. The song stays in C, where the band plays it.
rows.translation: Grunntónar og fimmundir eins og bassaleikari byrjar að styðja hljómsveit: grunntónn hljómsins þegar hann byrjar, fimmund hans á milli, lágt í fyrstu stöðu. Lagið helst í C þar sem hljómsveitin spilar það.
rows.context: Bass Songbook · Unit 1 · song bass-sb-song-mary “Mary Had a Little Lamb” · step 1 (explain) · lesson card text
